{
  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "scope_text": "For an employee of a covered employer seeking to qualify as an eligible employee.",
        "context_quotes": ["F003", "F004"],
        "modality_quote": "is",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F002", "F003", "F004"],
        "choice_quote": "F001:F004",
        "choice_text": "All three conditions must be satisfied: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules for airline flight crew employees); AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F002:F004",
        "references": ["§ 825.801", "§ 825.105(b)"],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005:F006"],
        "scope_text": "When counting the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted except as provided in paragraph (b)(2).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F006"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": ["paragraph (b)(2)"],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F007:F009"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months when an employment period precedes a break in service of more than seven years, where the break is occasioned by USERRA-covered service or where a written agreement exists concerning rehire.",
        "context_quotes": ["F008"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F008", "F009"],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": ["USERRA", "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation or where a written agreement (including a collective bargaining agreement) exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F008"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, where the employee had an absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": ["F008"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F008",
        "references": ["USERRA", "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F010"],
        "scope_text": "For an employee who is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; and for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "When an employer determines whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "Nothing in this section prevents",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": ["F012"],
        "modality_quote": "is determined",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["paragraph (c)(2)", "§ 825.801", "FLSA", "29 CFR part 785"],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work, based on the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA and not limited by methods of recordkeeping or non-reflective compensation agreements."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": ["FLSA"],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "In determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": ["F013"],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["USERRA", "§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining the employee's eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave, which are added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": ["F013"],
        "modality_quote": "can generally",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": ["USERRA", "§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F014"],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements under 29 CFR part 541.",
        "context_quotes": ["F014"],
        "modality_quote": "has the burden",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": ["FLSA", "29 CFR part 541", "§ 825.102", "§ 825.801(d)"],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim ineligibility."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "When making the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": ["F015"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.",
        "context_quotes": ["F015"],
        "modality_quote": "would be",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits based on whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles.",
        "context_quotes": ["F016"],
        "modality_quote": "is determined",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave, and once determined eligible in response to that notice, eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count within 75 miles for that specific notice."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "prohibition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F016"],
        "scope_text": "When employee FMLA leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.",
        "context_quotes": ["F016"],
        "modality_quote": "may not",
        "modality": "must_not",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50."
      }
    }
  ]

unit_attributes.scope_text: For an employee of a covered employer seeking to qualify as an eligible employee.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three conditions must be satisfied: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules for airline flight crew employees); AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When counting the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted except as provided in paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months when an employment period precedes a break in service of more than seven years, where the break is occasioned by USERRA-covered service or where a written agreement exists concerning rehire.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation or where a written agreement (including a collective bargaining agreement) exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, where the employee had an absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: For an employee who is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; and for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer determines whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work, based on the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA and not limited by methods of recordkeeping or non-reflective compensation agreements.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining the employee's eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave, which are added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements under 29 CFR part 541.
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim ineligibility.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When making the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: To ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits based on whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave, and once determined eligible in response to that notice, eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count within 75 miles for that specific notice.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When employee FMLA leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.
